deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A user says a site is down. What do you run first to test reachability?
note: Proves Layer 3 both directions. A failed ping does not prove the host is down — ICMP is often filtered.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to find where in the path latency starts. What do you run?
note: Latency that rises at a hop and stays high afterwards is the real problem hop.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A user can reach IPs but not names. What tool confirms it?
note: Query a public resolver and compare against yours.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need this PC's IP, mask, gateway and DNS. What do you run?
note: Also names the DHCP server that issued the lease.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A client is stuck with a bad DHCP lease. What do you run?
note: Forces the client to redo DORA.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: One PC still reaches an old server IP after a migration. What do you run?
note: Clears the local resolver cache. The population-wide fix is lowering the record TTL.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to know whether a service is listening on this server. What do you run?
note: Local sockets. LISTENING means the service is up.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You suspect a duplicate IP. What do you check first?
note: A flapping IP-to-MAC binding is the signature. Then trace the MAC on the switch.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to see the actual bytes on the wire. What do you use?
note: Needs a SPAN port or TAP to see traffic that is not yours.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to know which ports a remote server has open. What do you use?
note: Remote scanning. netstat is the local equivalent.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to know what device is plugged into a switch port. What do you use?
note: LLDP is the open standard (802.1AB); CDP is Cisco.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to find one cable in a bundle of 200. What tool?
note: Toner locates. A tester validates. They are not interchangeable.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to confirm a cable is wired to the right pins. What tool?
note: Continuity and pinout only — says nothing about performance.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A cable passes a continuity test but errors under load. What tool proves it?
note: Measures attenuation, NEXT and return loss against the TIA spec.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need the distance to a break in a fiber run. What tool?
note: TDR is the copper equivalent. The O is for optical.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need a quick check for a fiber break or bad splice. What tool?
note: Shoots visible red light down the fiber so faults glow.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: Wi-Fi is bad but there are no competing access points. What tool?
note: A Wi-Fi analyzer only sees Wi-Fi. A spectrum analyzer sees microwaves and cordless phones.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to see SSIDs, channels and signal strength. What tool?
note: Use it for channel overlap and coverage, not for non-Wi-Fi noise.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to know what is eating the bandwidth. What do you use?
note: Shows top talkers. A packet capture is the wrong tool for this question.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to measure real throughput between two internal hosts. What tool?
note: Lets you test one segment at a time and isolate the bottleneck.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to prove the carrier is the problem. Where and what do you test?
answer: Speed test at the demarc, plus traceroute
note: The demarc is the responsibility boundary. Test both sides of it.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need interface errors, duplex and utilization. What command?
note: Where cable faults and duplex mismatches become visible.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to map a MAC address to a physical port. What command?
note: How you trace a rogue device or a duplicate IP to a wall jack.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A device will not power up over PoE. What command?
note: Shows total budget, consumed watts and per-port draw.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You suspect the wrong switch became root bridge. What command?
note: Shows root bridge, port roles and port states.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to know why traffic takes an odd path. What command?
note: Also reveals whether a default route exists at all.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A link aggregation bundle will not come up. What command?
note: Reports which members are suspended and why.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to check VLAN membership per port. What command?

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A port is err-disabled. What do you do after fixing the cause?
note: Bouncing it without fixing the cause just repeats the violation.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need lossless traffic capture for forensics. SPAN or TAP?
note: A SPAN port can drop frames under load and hides physical-layer errors.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: A remote switch is unreachable after a config change. How do you get in?
answer: Out-of-band — console server or dedicated management port
note: In-band management dies with the network you just broke.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need per-hop packet loss over time, not a single snapshot. What tool?
note: Combines traceroute with sustained ping.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to know if a cable run exceeds 100 m. What tool?
note: A certifier reports the measured length along with pass/fail.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to test a port without another device. What tool?
note: Loops transmit back to receive.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to terminate a cable onto a patch panel. What tool?
note: 110 blocks are the modern data standard; 66 blocks are legacy voice.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to attach an RJ45 connector to a cable. What tool?

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to check whether a fiber is receiving enough light. What tool?
note: Confirms whether a transceiver is degrading.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to see which process is holding a port on Windows. What command?
note: Shows the owning executable.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need the routing table on a Windows host. What command?

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to test a specific TCP port from a client. What do you use?
note: Refused = nothing listening. Timeout = something is dropping.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to check a DNS record type such as MX. What do you run?
note: Mail problems are usually MX or PTR problems.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: You need to verify a change did not break anything else. What step is this?
note: Test the system, not just the original complaint.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: Your theory is that the carrier circuit is degraded, but you cannot test their gear. What now?
note: Escalation is legitimate at step 3 and step 5.

deck: N+ Quick · Tools and When to Use Them
front: An outage started at 09:00. Where do you look first?
note: Most incidents are caused by a change. Correlate by time.
